items.followUp: State Bohr’s postulates about electron orbits and the energy changes that occur when electrons move between orbits.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic arrangement of electrons in Bohr’s model.
rubric.description: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in definite circular orbits called shells.
rubric.how: State that electrons revolve around the nucleus in definite orbits or shells.

rubric.why: States that only permitted orbits have definite energies.
rubric.description: Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
rubric.how: Mention the definite energy of an allowed orbit.

rubric.why: States that an electron does not lose energy while remaining in an allowed orbit.
rubric.description: An electron in a permitted orbit does not radiate energy.
rubric.how: State that an electron does not radiate energy in an allowed orbit.

rubric.why: Describes energy changes during transitions between orbits.
rubric.description: An electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps between orbits; the energy change is ΔE = hν.
rubric.how: State that energy is absorbed or emitted in a transition and give the energy relation.

rubric.why: States the quantization condition for an electron’s angular momentum.
rubric.description: The angular momentum of an electron in an allowed orbit is quantized: mvr = nh/2π, where n is a whole number.
rubric.how: Give the quantized angular momentum condition or state that angular momentum is quantized.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in definite circular orbits called shells.
Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
An electron in a permitted orbit does not radiate energy.
An electron absorbs or emits energy when it jumps between orbits; the energy change is ΔE = hν.
The angular momentum of an electron in an allowed orbit is quantized: mvr = nh/2π, where n is a whole number.

items.followUp: Give four differences between an element and a compound.

rubric.why: Compares the proportions of components in compounds and mixtures.
rubric.description: A compound contains elements in a fixed ratio, whereas a mixture may contain its components in any proportion.
rubric.how: Contrast the fixed ratio in a compound with the variable proportions possible in a mixture.

rubric.why: Compares the properties of compounds and mixtures.
rubric.description: A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; mixture components retain their individual properties.
rubric.how: State that compounds have changed properties while mixture components retain their properties.

rubric.why: Compares how compounds and mixtures can be separated.
rubric.description: A compound can be separated into its elements by chemical methods; a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
rubric.how: Identify chemical methods for compounds and physical methods for mixtures.

rubric.why: Compares how the composition of each is represented.
rubric.description: A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no fixed chemical formula.
rubric.how: State that compounds have a definite formula while mixtures do not have a fixed formula.

modelAnswer: A compound contains elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio; a mixture may contain its components in any proportion.
A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; the components of a mixture retain their individual properties.
A compound can be separated into its elements by chemical methods; a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
A compound has a definite chemical formula; a mixture has no fixed chemical formula.

items.followUp: What is hydrogen bonding? Explain its occurrence between water molecules.

rubric.why: Defines the force and identifies the interacting parts of the polar molecules.
rubric.description: Dipole-dipole interaction is the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ends of neighbouring polar molecules.
rubric.how: Define it as an electrostatic attraction between opposite ends of polar molecules.

rubric.why: Identifies the partial charges on the atoms in HCl.
rubric.description: In HCl, hydrogen is partially positive and chlorine is partially negative: Hδ+—Clδ−.
rubric.how: Show or state the partial positive charge on hydrogen and the partial negative charge on chlorine.

rubric.why: Applies the interaction to neighbouring HCl molecules.
rubric.description: The Hδ+ end of one HCl molecule attracts the Clδ− end of a neighbouring HCl molecule.
rubric.how: Describe the attraction between opposite ends of adjacent HCl molecules.

rubric.why: Identifies that the interaction occurs between separate molecules.
rubric.description: The attraction between separate HCl molecules is an intermolecular dipole-dipole interaction.
rubric.how: State that the interaction is intermolecular.

modelAnswer: Dipole-dipole interaction is the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ends of neighbouring polar molecules.
In an HCl molecule, hydrogen has a partial positive charge and chlorine has a partial negative charge: Hδ+—Clδ−.
The Hδ+ end of one HCl molecule attracts the Clδ− end of a neighbouring HCl molecule.
This intermolecular attraction between separate HCl molecules is a dipole-dipole interaction.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a homogeneous mixture and a heterogeneous mixture, and state how they differ in composition.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining composition of a homogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout.
rubric.how: State that its composition is uniform throughout.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining composition of a heterogeneous mixture and distinguishes it from a homogeneous mixture.
rubric.description: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, with different parts distinguishable.
rubric.how: State that its composition is non-uniform and, optionally, give a suitable example.

modelAnswer: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout; for example, salt solution.
A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, with different parts distinguishable; for example, sand and water.
